title: Horace Henderson's small-group records with Red Allen and Hawkins
summary: Jones first really listened to Red on records by a Horace Henderson group with Red, Hilton Jefferson and Benny Morton, and still owns the discs, as well as Red's own sessions with Coleman Hawkins.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: He played good there. But when I really started to listen to him, he was playing in a band -- playing in a group, and I think it was a group -- I can't think what they called them now, but it was Horace Henderson. It could have been his Stompers or something, Horace Henderson's Stompers.
Yeah.
But he would have Red and Hilton Jefferson.
Yeah.
And I don't know who was on -- oh, and Benny Morton on trombone.
Really?
Yeah. I have a few of the old 78s of that.
Have you?
I brought them with me from Buffalo.
Is that right.
Yeah, so we used to sit in Buffalo and listen to this all the time. Thought how great he was you
know, and oh, there were some good things made with that little group. Not to be popular, you know, but --
Yeah, I know what you mean. Good, swinging music.
Yeah, good, swinging music.
Yeah.
And they had -- they must have had maybe a half a dozen sessions.
Well, I was going to say, you see, Red made some under his own name.
Yeah.
Which were very good.
Yes, he did.
Which he sang the vocals on, because I guess in those days they thought it was commercial for him to do it.
Then they had someone called Allen [Coleman Hawkins] Hawkins, when Hawk played with him.
That's right, yes.
I've got all that stuff.
That's good.
Yeah, I have it on records.
